-76.66110,40.27020.name: Penn State Milton S. Hershey Medical Center
-76.66110,40.27020.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Samantha Butts, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-43.94509,-19.92273.name: Fertibaby Medicina Reprodutiva
-43.94509,-19.92273.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: http://fertibaby.com.br/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

-78.87078,42.89772.name: ZeptoMetrix Corp
-78.87078,42.89772.state: 878 Main St, Buffalo, NY 14202, United States, United States
-78.87078,42.89772.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by ZeptoMetrix Corp. It is categorised as a private laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-0.36000,51.81000.name: Rothamsted Research
-0.36000,51.81000.desc: The oldest agricultural research station in the world, running field experiments that have continued since the 1840s and conducting engineered wheat and camelina trials. Its long-term experiments are the reference dataset against which agricultural change is measured, engineered or otherwise.

6.21000,46.43120.name: IUCN — synthetic biology and biodiversity conservation
6.21000,46.43120.desc: The world conservation union’s position process on synthetic biology, which took years and split its membership. It is the most thorough attempt anywhere to reach a conservation position on engineered organisms, and it ended without prohibiting the tools.

-71.21300,42.48200.name: Conagen
-71.21300,42.48200.desc: Produces flavour, fragrance and sweetener compounds by fermenting engineered microbes instead of extracting them from plants. A vanilla or stevia molecule made this way is chemically identical to the plant-derived one and can often be labelled natural, which means the substitution reaches a shelf with nothing to distinguish it — and the farmers who grew the original crop lose the market without any decision being announced.

-92.94750,17.98920.name: Congreso del Estado de Tabasco
-92.94750,17.98920.desc: The state legislature that wrote the law which made Tabasco the destination for cross-border surrogacy in Mexico, and then voted 21 to 9 to close it to foreign intended parents and to male same-sex couples, restricting the arrangement to Mexican couples including a woman aged 25 to 40 able to show she was medically unable to bear a child. A state assembly in one Mexican state was, for a period, effectively setting the terms of an international market — and the restriction it passed was later displaced by the supreme court. Both directions of travel happened in the same country within five years, which is why this facet needs the legislatures recorded and not only the agencies.
